title: Document 1 — Applicant information | Reshelve Cabinetry Workshop
titleZh: 文件 1｜申請須知｜瑞雪夫木作工場
passage:
We have two three-week placements in February. The first is for people learning to prepare a project for cutting; the second is for people who already cut accurately and want to alter plans when a customer changes a requirement. Applicants may list both preferences, but they can be interviewed for only one placement.

For either placement, submit one photo of work that you did yourself. For the plan-adjustment placement, include an earlier drawing and a short note explaining what changed after that drawing was made. The picture does not need to be of a finished cabinet; clamps, a fitted divider, or scrap pieces used to test a joint can provide the evidence. A photograph of work done by a classmate does not meet the requirement, even if your instructor helps you describe it. If the change is about how a part moves, a photo of your bench trial is fine. It must show the part in the position that made the difference, with the same obstruction or limit that the customer has. A photograph of the work at rest may not show this.

We read the note and look at the photo together. If the earlier drawing and note are missing, an application listing the cutting placement second can still be considered for that placement as long as its photo qualifies. We will not ask applicants to send missing drawings after the closing date. Please keep the actual work; nothing needs to be brought to the first interview. If you kept several versions, send the drawing that shows the plan immediately before the change you describe. A later drawing can be useful in the shop, but it does not show the decision you were working from. The note should say why you changed that decision.

Here is an example. Nell first drew a shallow shelf and then made it deeper to take the customer’s books. She traced that approved drawing onto a fresh sheet and tried putting the hinge on the other side in pencil. She put that idea aside without using it. When she tried the approved layout beside the customer’s wall pipe, the open door hit the pipe. Moving the hinge inward let the door clear it. Nell built a scrap frame herself and set a wooden block at the pipe’s position. The block sits at the same distance from the cabinet as the real pipe.
passageZh:
我們在二月開設兩個為期三週的實習。第一個適合想學習如何準備裁切工序的人；第二個適合已能精準裁切、想學習如何在客戶改變要求時調整計畫的人。申請人可以把兩個實習都列入志願，但只會受邀面試其中一個。

不論申請哪個實習，都要提交一張照片，內容須是你親手做的作品。若申請計畫調整實習，還要附上較早的圖面，並簡短說明畫出那張圖之後改了什麼。照片不必拍完整的櫃子；夾具、裝好的隔板或用來測試接合的邊角料，都可以作為證明。即使老師幫你撰寫說明，若照片是同學的作品，仍不符合要求。 如果變更和零件的移動方式有關，你可以提交自己在工作臺上試作的照片。照片須呈現有關鍵差異的位置，以及與客戶現場相同的障礙物或限制。零件靜止放著時拍的照片，不一定看得出差異。

我們會一起看說明與照片。若未附較早的圖面與說明，而第二志願是裁切實習，只要照片符合要求，仍可列入該實習的審查。報名截止後，不會再請申請人補交缺失的圖面。請自行保留實物；第一次面試不需要帶作品來。 若保留了好幾個版本，請提交做出你要說明的變更之前、當時採用的那張圖。較晚畫的圖在工場或許有用，但看不出你原先依據的是什麼。附註應說明為何改變那個決定。

舉個例子。妮爾先畫了較淺的層板，後來為了放客戶的書把層板加深。她把那份核准的圖描到新紙上，試著用鉛筆把鉸鏈移到另一側，但沒有採用那個構想。她依核准的配置在客戶的牆管旁試用時，門一打開就撞到管子。把鉸鏈往內移後，門就能避開它。妮爾親手用邊角料做了試驗框架，並在管子的位置放了一塊木塊。木塊到櫃體的距離和現場的管子相同。
